headline: NEW -- Brent touches $115.16 (highest since May 4) as Ansar Allah launch fresh attack wave on Saudi Arabia incl. claimed Yanbu
dek: Brent crude futures touched $115.16 intraday (+1.5-1.65%), highest since May 4; WTI $101.27-101.30. Drivers: Ansar Allah-claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil loading port, Aramco facilities, Shaybah oilfield, Dammam/King Fahd airport over past 48h; Libya pipeline-valve closure curtailing…
sources: Reuters (Stephanie Kelly) + The National + Ansar Allah military spokesman claim (Yanbu)
fault_line: "Who pays for the war?" -- blame Ansar Allah/Iran for driving fuel prices vs. blame Trump's Russia diesel deal for enriching adversaries while US consumers face record diesel prices.

sections.what_happened: Brent crude futures touched $115.16 intraday (+1.5-1.65%), highest since May 4; WTI $101.27-101.30. Drivers: Ansar Allah-claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil loading port, Aramco facilities, Shaybah oilfield, Dammam/King Fahd airport over past 48h; Libya pipeline-valve closure curtailing production; UBS: 'worst-case renewed supply disruptions' risk keeps market undersupplied; Brent set for third straight weekly gain (+4.4%); ING dropped its $80 Q4 Brent-average forecast as unattainable.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (Euronext live feed): $115.16 print; The National: $115 at 17:26 with MUFG quote ('Oil prices remain supported by geopolitical risks...'); CNA: same Reuters wire. Ansar Allah Yanbu/Shaybah claims are ATTRIBUTED (Ansar Allah spokesman), consistent with the pattern of Saudi-confirmed casualties at Dammam/Shaybah reported in earlier scans. NYT (via Reuters/CNBC-TV18): US and Israel planning renewed Iran strikes after Nov 3 midterms adds the risk premium.
sections.what_disputed: Ansar Allah strike claims on Yanbu/Shaybah unconfirmed by Saudi authorities; ING analysts note the Friday move extended the run but contract later changed hands ~$110.39; Strait of Hormuz flows recovering toward pre-war levels, so supply is tightened rather than cut.
sections.why_matters: Highest oil price in five months while Trump's Russian diesel tanker is still 15 days from New York -- the pocketbook story that connects the war room to the petrol station. Lead with the number on screen, then the Yanbu claim.
sections.context: Background: NEW -- Brent touches $115.16 (highest since May 4) as Ansar Allah launch fresh attack wave on Saudi Arabia incl. claimed Yanbu oil-loading-port strike

totw_analysis: Our read: Highest oil price in five months while Trump's Russian diesel tanker is still 15 days from New York -- the pocketbook story that connects the war room to the petrol station. Lead with the number on screen, then the Yanbu claim. The fault line our audience is arguing over: "Who pays for the war?" -- blame Ansar Allah/Iran for driving fuel prices vs. blame Trump's Russia diesel deal for enriching adversaries while US consumers face record diesel prices.
